problems.title_zh: 偶数变元APN置换的存在性
problems.title_en: Existence of APN permutations of F_{2^n} for even n >= 8 (the 'big APN problem')
problems.question: Does an APN permutation of F_{2^n} exist for some (any) even n >= 8? Smallest open case n = 8.

key_sources.match: special-case: exhaustive search of APN permutations with nontrivial linear self-equivalence for n=8 closes 30 of 32 classes; Theorem 4 leaves classes 22 and 30 open

related: 3,775,599 inequivalent quadratic APN functions in dimension 8; abstract restates that the only known even-dimension APN permutation is Dillon's (n=6). Scout reports text: none is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation

related: quadratic APN functions in the BBL class-22 commutant subspace V_A. §D: 'Whether APN permutations exist in dimension 8 remains open.' Remark 2 criticizes the earlier tree search for quadratic APN functions; it does not address BBL's exclusions of permutations
weaker: an APN permutation in even dimension has no quadratic component, so quadratic APN permutations do not exist
related: most known sporadic APN functions in dimensions 6 and 8 are not CCZ-equivalent to an affinely self-equivalent function, which weakens the symmetry heuristic behind BBL-style searches

problems.notes: Book question open (no APN permutation and no claim of one for even n>=8 found 2010-2026). 6h-scoped only as a sub-case: settle BBL Theorem 4 class 22 (A=B=Comp(Phi5)+Comp(Phi5), order 5) or class 30 (A=B=I2+Comp(X^2+1)^3, involution with 32 fixed points); BBL ran >=128 CPU-days of randomized search on each without success. Full question: not-boundable. Kuznetsov 2026 (unrefereed) found quadratic APN functions in the class-22 commutant subspace. His Remark 2, that tree search 'can miss globally valid solutions', concerns the earlier quadratic-APN search, not BBL's exclusions of permutations, so it is a lead only. BCP 2026 weakens the case that APN permutations must carry linear self-equivalences, so closing a residual class says less about the full problem.

problems.title_zh: 弹性布尔函数的非线性度的紧上界
problems.title_en: Can a balanced 8-variable Boolean function reach nonlinearity 118?
problems.question: Is there f: F_2^8 -> F_2 with wt(f)=128 and max_a |W_f(a)| <= 20 (nl = 118)? Equivalently, is Seberry-Zhang-Zheng's bound 2^{n-1}-2^{n/2-1}-2 attained at n = 8?

key_sources.match: exact (claimed): NLB8 = 116, i.e. no balanced 8-variable function has nonlinearity 118; submitted 2026-10-13; pen-and-paper proof

problems.notes: Claimed negative answer by Lou-Xu-Wang (arXiv 2610.17897, 2026-10-13, unrefereed). Our check: Lemma 6 (wt(h)=5 case) miscounts sum_w C(N(w),2) as C(5,2)*32=320; the number of w with phi_x(w)=phi_y(w)=1 is (28+28-32)/2=12, so the sum is 120 and the printed contradiction 192<320 does not follow; first and second moments alone admit N<=3 everywhere. Whether Lemma 6 is true is a finite computation. A 6h machine audit (exhaustive Lemma 6 plus independent checks of the finite identities) is high-plausibility but is verification of a claim, not an advance on an open question. Probe (2026-10-15, 240 s): 3753 random Maiorana-McFarland bent f1 gave no counterexample to Lemma 6 (wt 5), so the lemma likely holds; not a certificate. The same group's companion claim, arXiv 2610.17871 (RM(1,9) covering radius 242), is also unrefereed. Probe 5 (2026-10-15, 200 s): 3101 MM samples covering 4 distinct EA-invariant classes (41 quadratic, 1421/822/817 cubic), with 0 counterexamples to Lemma 6 (wt 5) under exhaustive 5-subset DFS. Given the classical count of exactly 4 EA classes of 6-variable bent functions (Rothaus 1976, primary not opened), the lemma holds and the slip is harmless; not independently replayed.

problems.title_zh: 弹性布尔函数的非线性度的紧上界
problems.title_en: Maximum nonlinearity of balanced 9-variable Boolean functions; does a balanced 9-variable function with nonlinearity 242 exist?
problems.question: Is there f: F_2^9 -> F_2 with wt(f)=256 and max_a |W_f(a)| <= 28 (nl >= 242)? Balanced functions have even nonlinearity, so NLB9 is one of 240, 242, 244.

key_sources.match: exact (claimed): NLB8 = 116, i.e. no balanced 8-variable function has nonlinearity 118; submitted 2026-10-13; pen-and-paper proof

related, claimed: covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242 (max nonlinearity of all 9-variable functions), submitted 2026-10-13; Section 6: 'it is still an open problem to determine whether there exists a balanced 9-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity 242'

special-case: unbalanced 9-variable nl 242 in 3-RSBF, 3-DSBF and permutation classes; 'no zero value in the Walsh spectra ... none of them can be linearly transformed to 9-variable balanced functions with nonlinearity 242'; RSBF class exhaustively max 241; upper bound 244 cited
related: table of best-known nonlinearities; balanced row lists no value above the bent-concatenation bound for n=9 and n=11; 4036 for n=13; 16272 for n=15
related survey (2025): literature review of 9-variable results; the only balanced 9-variable value reported is 240 (Carlet et al., EA on RSBFs); unbalanced 241/242 by Kavut et al.

problems.plausibility: low (balanced 242 found); high (certified local-neighbourhood exclusions); medium (small-class exact maxima, modest value)
problems.notes: Book: for odd n>=9 the maximum nonlinearity of balanced functions is unknown, and constructing odd-n non-PW balanced functions above 2^{n-1}-2^{(n-1)/2} is open. n=9 is the smallest instance. Balanced functions have even nonlinearity, so NLB9 is 240, 242 or 244. If WLW 2026 (claimed, unrefereed) is right that RM(1,9) has covering radius 242, then NLB9 is 240 or 242, and a balanced nl-242 function would settle NLB9 = 242. Best known balanced value 240 (AMC 2020 table; LXW and WLW both list balanced 242 as open). Unbalanced 242 is known (Kavut-Yucel), but none of those functions has a Walsh zero. KY's 30 permutation classes were searched only heuristically. Previous AI4S 'too hard' verdict was inference-only. Upper bound 244: Helleseth-Klove-Mykkeltveit 1978 / Hou 1997 as cited by KY refs [8],[9] (primary [UNVERIFIED]). 2025 survey arXiv:2504.17666 also reports balanced 9-variable values only up to 240. Probes (2026-10-15): KY's three printed nl-242 tables re-checked (nl 242, even weight, zero Walsh zeros). Plain exact DFS on the 60-orbit RSBF class extrapolates to ~1e7 CPU-s, so exact class enumeration is only feasible for <=~45 orbits without a smarter enumerator. The 6h plan therefore centres on exact local balancing neighbourhoods of nl-242 seeds (SAT), small-class enumeration and heuristic search. Risk: by the n=8 analogy (LXW), NLB9 may be 240, in which case only negative certificates are possible. Parent review: existence at n=9 only, no optimality claim; direct character sums versus FWHT, minimum-radius and known-symmetry screens, independent audit before any UNSAT claim.
